mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically from -10.0 to -5.9 over four weeks, indicating a consistent recovery trend. This momentum will persist over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC further positive relative to the baseline mean of the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 4.1 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days falls below the mean of the last 28 days (-8.0), or declines week-on-week in three of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains elevated and stable (37.0 to 40.7 range), signaling sustained essential-goods purchasing behavior. This behavioral lock-in reduces discretionary retail trips, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth below the prior four-week mean.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 35 for all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the prior 28-day mean by more than 2 percentage points, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below 30 in any of the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has stabilized near -4.3 (t-0w), indicating commuting patterns are no longer deteriorating. When transit stabilization occurs, retail footfall follows within two weeks as workers resume incidental shopping during commute windows.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change is less than 1 point in absolute value
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -10.4 to -4.3 over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior four-week mean within two weeks, or TRANSIT falls more than 3 points in any single week.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has recovered from -23.6 to -15.7 over four weeks, indicating outdoor recreation is normalizing. This signals reduced lockdown severity; retail-and-recreation venues will follow the same relaxation trajectory, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 7.9 points over four weeks
failure_condition: PARKS and RETAIL_REC do not move in the same direction over the next four weeks, or PARKS reverts below -20.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has stabilized at 5.3-5.9 over the last three weeks, indicating people are no longer increasing home time. Combined with WORKPLACES stabilization near -2.3, this signals the end of lockdown-driven behavior; retail will rebound as people resume normal activity patterns.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL week-on-week change is less than 0.5 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL variance < 1.0 over last two weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rises above 7.0 in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines relative to the prior four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has recovered from -13.6 to -2.3 over three weeks, crossing a critical threshold indicating return-to-office policies are taking effect. When workplace return exceeds -5 points, retail footfall follows within one week as office workers resume shopping patterns.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES exceeds -5.0 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 11.3 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within one week of WORKPLACES exceeding -5.0, or WORKPLACES falls below -8.0 in the next week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and PARKS mobility are both recovering (TRANSIT: -10.4 to -4.3; PARKS: -23.6 to -15.7), indicating seasonal reopening of outdoor and transit-dependent activities. This dual recovery signals a seasonal shift that will drive retail-and-recreation mobility upward over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and PARKS improve by more than 1.0 point week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and PARKS both show consistent improvement
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or PARKS reverts to prior-week levels in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not exceed the prior four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has plateaued at 39.4 (t-0w) after rising to 40.7 (t-1w), indicating saturation of essential-goods purchasing. As grocery demand stabilizes, consumers will redirect discretionary spending to retail-and-recreation venues, suppressing relative RETAIL_REC growth if grocery remains elevated, or accelerating it if grocery begins to decline.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains between 38 and 41 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM plateau at 39.4 after peak of 40.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises more than 3 points relative to the prior four-week mean within two weeks, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below 35.
